--- title: bc.b format: html: css: /man.css --- ## Broadcasted Boolean Operations {.unnumbered} ### Description The bc.b() method performs broadcasted logical (or Boolean) operations on 2 arrays.

Please note that these operations will treat the input as logical.
Therefore, something like bc.b(1, 2, "==") returns TRUE, because both 1 and 2 are TRUE when treated as logical.

For regular relational operators, see [bc.rel](bc.rel.qmd).

### Usage 
bc.b(x, y, op, ...)

## S4 method for signature 'ANY'
bc.b(x, y, op)
### Arguments
x, y conformable vectors/arrays of type logical, numeric, or raw.
Note that input with type of double will be coerced to integer.
op a single string, giving the operator.
Supported Boolean operators: &, |, xor, nand, nor, ==, !=, <, >, <=, >=.
"nand" is defined here as !(x & y), and "nor" is defined here as !(x | y).
... further arguments passed to or from methods.

### Details bc.b() efficiently casts the input to logical.
Since the input is treated as logical, the following equalities hold for bc.b():
  • "==" is equivalent to !xor(x, y), but faster;
  • "!=" is equivalent to xor(x, y);
  • "<" is equivalent to (!x & y), but faster;
  • ">" is equivalent to (x & !y), but faster;
  • "<=" is equivalent to (!x & y) | (y == x), but faster;
  • ">=" is equivalent to (x & !y) | (y == x), but faster.
Note that the above equalities only hold in the absence of NAs, since the & and | operators handle NAs differently than the relational operators.

### Value Normally:
A logical array/vector as a result of the broadcasted Boolean operation.

If both x and y are type of raw:
A raw array/vector as a result of the broadcasted Boolean operation, where 01 codes for TRUE and 00 codes for FALSE.
This is convenient as raw requires less memory space than logical.

### See Also [broadcast_operators](aaa01_broadcast_operators.qmd)
### Examples ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library("broadcast") x.dim <- c(4:2) x.len <- prod(x.dim) x.data <- sample(c(TRUE, FALSE, NA), x.len, TRUE) x <- array(x.data, x.dim) y <- array(1:50, c(4,1,1)) bc.b(x, y, "&") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA FALSE TRUE #> [2,] FALSE NA TRUE #> [3,] FALSE TRUE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE TRUE NA #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA TRUE NA #> [2,] NA NA TRUE #> [3,] FALSE NA TRUE #> [4,] FALSE NA FALSE bc.b(x, y, "|") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [2,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [3,] TRUE TRUE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE TRUE TRUE bc.b(x, y, "xor") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA TRUE FALSE #> [2,] TRUE NA FALSE #> [3,] TRUE FALSE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE FALSE NA #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA FALSE NA #> [2,] NA NA FALSE #> [3,] TRUE NA FALSE #> [4,] TRUE NA TRUE bc.b(x, y, "nand") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA TRUE FALSE #> [2,] TRUE NA FALSE #> [3,] TRUE FALSE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE FALSE NA #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA FALSE NA #> [2,] NA NA FALSE #> [3,] TRUE NA FALSE #> [4,] TRUE NA TRUE bc.b(x, y, "==") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA FALSE TRUE #> [2,] FALSE NA TRUE #> [3,] FALSE TRUE FALSE #> [4,] FALSE TRUE NA #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA TRUE NA #> [2,] NA NA TRUE #> [3,] FALSE NA TRUE #> [4,] FALSE NA FALSE bc.b(x, y, "!=") #> , , 1 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA TRUE FALSE #> [2,] TRUE NA FALSE #> [3,] TRUE FALSE TRUE #> [4,] TRUE FALSE NA #> #> , , 2 #> #> [,1] [,2] [,3] #> [1,] NA FALSE NA #> [2,] NA NA FALSE #> [3,] TRUE NA FALSE #> [4,] TRUE NA TRUE ``` :::
